description: Cross-site scripting found by a policy written for operating-system shells, with no policy change at all: a browser parsing a response body is an interpreter, so describing the channel was the whole of it. Four routes pin the four distinctions that matter. Unescaped interpolation is a finding. The same value through escape-html is not, because the escaper addresses the context that applies. The same value through res.json is not, because a JSON body is not parsed as markup. The same value through encodeURIComponent IS, because a URL encoder is not an HTML encoder and must be recorded as considered-and-insufficient rather than silently clearing.

expected.note: interpolated into a text/html response body
a URL encoder does not neutralize markup
